Diatribe

DYE-uh-tribe · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Diatribe is a forceful and bitter verbal attack.

The op-ed was less an argument than a diatribe against the entire industry.

Worked Example

His email turned into a five-paragraph diatribe against every decision the company had made that year.

A forceful, bitter, sweeping written attack -- not a calm critique -- is exactly what a diatribe is.

How Diatribe Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

tirade

tirade: a long, angry speech of criticism, close synonym

rant

rant: an emotional, often disorganized outburst of criticism

Antonyms

tribute

tribute: a statement of respect or admiration

praise

praise: an expression of approval

How Strong Is It? — criticism → diatribe → tirade

criticism vs. diatribe

criticism vs. diatribe: Criticism can be measured and fair; a diatribe is a forceful, bitter, one-sided verbal attack.

tirade vs. diatribe

tirade vs. diatribe: Tirade is close to diatribe, though it often feels even more emotionally uncontrolled and less carefully argued.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — dia-

prefix — dia-: through, across (Greek)

root — tribe

root — tribe: to rub, wear down (Greek (tribein))

Put it together

Put it together: dia- ('through, across') + tribe ('to rub, wear down') together suggest an argument that wears its target down -- the forceful, bitter attack a diatribe delivers.

Use the root in a new word: tribulation

Use the root in a new word: tribulation: Tribulation comes from the same Greek/Latin root, tribein/tribulare ('to rub, to grind down'), which also runs beneath diatribe.
